title: contextual-latency-ratio-rollback-guard: add cohort-aware ratio detector and traffic-weighted cooldown
author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Motivation and summary:
This PR introduces a new cohort-aware detector (Contextual Latency Ratio Detector) and a ratio-based rollback guard that aims to detect regression signals that appear only in specific traffic cohorts (client SDK version, request size bucket, or routing tag). The detector computes robust ratios (e.g., P95 / median) per cohort and compares them against historically bootstrapped baselines with traffic-weighted confidence. When a cohort shows a statistically significant increase in the ratio for sustained windows, the rollout guard can throttle or rollback the canary in a traffic-weighted manner rather than a binary global abort.

Key reasons for this approach:
- Some regressions are cohort-localized (e.g., long-sequence requests or a particular client SDK). Global quantile checks miss these early signals.
- Ratio-based signals normalize against distributional shifts in medians (helpful when overall median moves due to legitimate load pattern changes).
- Traffic-weighted cooldown avoids oscillation by gating action on the relative traffic impact of the failing cohort.

What this PR adds (high level):
- perf_canary/detectors/contextual_ratio_detector.py: new detector implementation with bootstrap baseline, cohort hashing, and ratio computation.
- perf_canary/configs/ratio_guard.yaml: runtime config for detector thresholds, minimum cohort size, persistence window, and traffic-weighted cooldown parameters.
- perf_canary/core/aggregation.py: small helper additions to support per-cohort incremental aggregation and percentile sketches used by the detector.
- perf_canary/tests/test_contextual_ratio_detector.py: unit + small integration tests using synthetic traffic with injected regressions.
- docs/observability/ratio-guard.md: user-facing docs describing detector semantics and suggested thresholds.
- dashboards/ratio-guard-panel.json: dashboard panel for cohort heatmap + ratio trend.
- k8s/perf-canary-configmap.yaml: new configmap entries to wire the detector in canary deployments.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration test against perf-canary simulation harness
- [x] Documentation and dashboard panels
- [x] Smoke e2e on staging canary pipeline

Implementation notes:
- Cohorts are defined by a configurable set of request attributes; default: [client_sdk, sequence_length_bucket, routing_tag]. Cohort hashing uses a stable 64-bit hash to bucket low-cardinality attributes and a thresholded fallback for high-cardinality keys.
- For each cohort we maintain median and p95 estimates with QuantileSketch and obtain a bootstrapped historical distribution over the ratio R = p95 / median using reservoir sampling over daily aggregates. Alerting compares the current cohort ratio to the bootstrap percentile and uses a Wilson score inspired confidence correction to account for small cohort sizes.
- The guard evaluates cohorts every 30s. If multiple cohorts exceed the configured ratio_threshold for more than N consecutive windows and the aggregated traffic share of failing cohorts exceeds traffic_share_threshold, the guard triggers traffic reduction steps (proportional throttles) up to a configured max rollback.
- To avoid noise, we only consider cohorts with min_requests_per_window and require a silence window after corrective action unless a fresh regression emerges.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- The detector is off by default. Operators enable it by adding the ratio_guard configmap keys. No change to default canary behavior.
- Config values use conservative defaults; recommended thresholds are documented in docs/observability/ratio-guard.md.

Related work and references:
- ENG-4128: explore cohort-aware canary detectors
- ENG-4199: traffic-weighted rollback strategy design doc
- Prior detectors (temporal-fingerprint, multiscale-fingerprint) detect different signal families; this ratio-based approach complements them by normalizing for median shifts.

review_comments: Diego Martínez (reviewer): This looks promising. Please add a follow-up note that documents how the cohort hashing behaves for high-cardinality user ids—right now implementation drops to 'other' bucket but we need an operator knob.
Alyssa Chen (author): Good catch — added min_cardinality_threshold and explicit fallback policy in config. See perf_canary/configs/ratio_guard.yaml commit.
Priya Rao (reviewer): Can you add a benchmark for detector CPU overhead on the 95th percentile path? We should ensure this can run in our sidecar at 1QPS per core.
Alyssa Chen (author): Added micro-benchmarks in scripts/bench/cohort_sim.py and documented expected CPU per 10k reqs/s in README. Benchmarks show ~6% CPU at our default sketch config.
Liam O'Neill (approver): Verified behavior in staging pipeline and dashboard; minor nit on log verbosity fixed. Approving for merge.
release_notes: Add new contextual latency ratio detector and traffic-weighted rollback guard (off by default). Operators can enable via perf_canary configmap and tune cohort attributes and thresholds.
notes_for_ops: To enable: add perf-canary configmap keys (see k8s/perf-canary-configmap.yaml). Suggested conservative thresholds are in docs/observability/ratio-guard.md. Monitor cohort heatmap dashboard and noise metrics (cohort_counts, bootstrap_confidence).
testing_done: Unit tests + integration harness with synthetic injected regressions. Staging e2e smoke passed. Performed microbenchmarks for CPU and memory impact; results in perf_canary/bench/README.md.
known_issues: High-cardinality cohorts can underpower bootstrap confidence; the config currently collapses rare keys into 'other' with a minimum cohort-size gate. Follow-up ENG task recommended to add dynamic cohort merging heuristics.
